subject: EdgeFin perf follow-up: TTFT targets & streaming options
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@edgefin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 16:12:00 -0500
Subject: Follow-up & quick clarifications from today's perf discussion

Hi Alex / Samira —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap + two concrete asks so our engineering team can scope the pilot: 

Call highlights (short):
- Goal: embed streaming summarization into EdgeFin mobile app; primary UX metric is perceived response time.
- Target: customer expects first visible token quickly so users feel the app is "responding" immediately.
- Traffic shape: steady daytime traffic with two short bursts during market opens.

Open items we discussed that would change our proposal: 
1) Target TTFT (time-to-first-token) SLA you want us to commit to (95th pct / p99). You mentioned 300ms feels ideal on mobile — can you confirm if 95th pct @ 300ms is acceptable, or do you want 250ms?
2) Streaming transport preference: do you need WebSocket support for mobile apps, or would SSE + a small WebSocket fallback be acceptable given mobile proxy behaviour?
3) Chunk cadence: preference for smaller chunks (~40–80 tokens) vs larger chunks (150–250 tokens) — smaller improves perceived smoothness but can increase server-side overhead.

Immediate asks: 
- Please confirm the TTFT SLA target (95th and p99 if possible).
- Confirm preferred transport (SSE primary / WebSocket primary / both).

I've attached a short SLO proposal and a technical note on chunk cadence that shows cost/latency tradeoffs (redwood-slo-proposal.pdf, streaming-pacing-proposal.md). Ben is copied to scope an engineering sync once we have your answers.

Next step: If you confirm targets, Ben and I can put together a one-week pilot plan with a small dedicated pool and an integration checklist.

Best,
Nikhil
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

attachments: redwood-slo-proposal.pdf (application/pdf), streaming-pacing-proposal.md (text/markdown)

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@edgefin.com>

Cc: Samira Patel <samira.patel@edgefin.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 09:07:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up & quick clarifications from today's perf discussion

Hi Nikhil —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline below.

TTFT: we want the experience to feel instant on mobile. Our engineering bar is 250ms at 95th, 450ms at p99. We're happy to start with a 95th @ 250ms pilot target and measure p99 during the pilot.

Transport: mobile clients go through a handful of corporate proxies and some older Android builds that chunk WebSocket libraries — our preference is WebSocket as primary for mobile (more reliable with intermittent connectivity), but SSE would be fine for server-to-server calls. In short: WebSocket-first for mobile SDKs, SSE OK for backend integrations.

Chunk cadence: UX team favors many small chunks — they believe even 30–60 token increments feel most responsive for users skimming live output. If smaller chunks materially increase cost, tell us the tradeoff and we'll prioritize.

We can do a technical sync Thurs 11am ET with Ben and your infra lead. Also included Samira (product) — she'll own the pilot acceptance criteria.

Thanks —
Alex
Principal Product Manager, EdgeFin

Note: forward any architecture docs or pilot runbooks to samira.patel@edgefin.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@edgefin.com>, Samira Patel <samira.patel@edgefin.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 08:33:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up & quick clarifications from today's perf discussion

Alex / Samira —

Appreciate the clear targets — that helps. A few technical notes and our recommended pilot configuration to hit 95th @ 250ms: 

Short technical notes:
- TTFT physics: with a GPU-optimized runtime we expect cold-starts to dominate p99; for 95th-level latency the biggest levers are warm workers, connection reuse, and small prompt priming.
- Transport: WebSocket-first for mobile is sensible. Redwood supports both WS and SSE; we recommend WS for mobile because it keeps a persistent TCP connection (fewer reprovisions via proxies) and allows us to reduce handshake overhead. We'll enable SSE for backend traffic where connection semantics are simpler.
- Chunk cadence: to match the UX ask (~30–60 tokens), we propose server-side pacing of ~50-token chunks with an adaptive window (grow to 120 tokens if the model can stream larger segments without hurting latency). This balances perceived responsiveness and per-token CPU overhead.

Pilot proposal (one-week):
- Dedicated minimal cluster: 1x reserved T4x2 equivalent pool to keep KV cache warm (warm workers reduce cold-starts).
- Autoscale policy: rapid scale to handle market-open bursts with a 30s scale-in delay to avoid churn.
- Observability: token-level latency traces + per-connection first-byte timings; we'll generate a daily dashboard and a CSV export for your telemetry team.
- Acceptance criteria: 95th <= 250ms for at least 48 consecutive hours of steady traffic; functional streaming behavior on iOS/Android SDKs (WS).

Attachments: I attached a one-page pilot runbook and a short checklist (edgefin-integration-checklist.xlsx).

Next steps: Confirm Thurs 11am ET for tech sync. If you want, we can include an optional procurement touchpoint to discuss reserved capacity pricing.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks all —

This matches our expectations. Confirming:
- Pilot targets: 95th <= 250ms; will monitor p99 but won't block pilot acceptance unless p99 > 1s for sustained periods.
- Transport: WebSocket primary for mobile, SSE for server-side.
- Chunk cadence: aim for 50-token pacing with adaptive growth to 120 tokens when CPU suggests it's OK.

We accept the proposed one-week pilot. Please send the runbook and a calendar invite for Thurs 11am ET technical sync (include your infra/ops lead if possible). Also send any sample SDK snippets for WebSocket integration so our mobile engineers can pre-review.

Samira Patel
Director, Product Operations | EdgeFin
